the study of the pathogenesis of experimental hypertension.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increased DOC and progesterone levels are not a cause of hypertension in the MtT/F4 rat, and that the elevated corticosterone level is a consequence of the hypertension.
plasma steroids are altered in rats with experimental arterial hypertension due to an ectopic pituitory tumor, and that the increased DOC concentration in plasma plays a role in this pathogenesis.
the increased plasma levels of DOC in rats with ectopic MtT/F4 tumor are not the result of increased production of DOC in the adrenal cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the MtT/F4 rat model, the increased DOC levels are responsible for the hypertension, and the increased plasma progesterone is a secondary phenomenon, probably due to the stimulation of adrenal steroidogenesis by the increased DOC levels.
in rats bearing the MtT/F4 tumor, the adrenal gland was enlarged and showed a marked increase of the zona glomerulosa, but the zona fasciculata and reticularis were not enlarged.
